facts.statement: The animal belongs to the genus Deinocheirus.
facts.quote: genus: Deinocheirus

facts.statement: The only known species is Deinocheirus mirificus.
facts.quote: species: mirificus

facts.statement: The genus was named by Osmólska and Roniewicz in 1970.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Osmólska & Roniewicz, 1970

facts.statement: Deinocheirus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus ( ) is a genus of large ornithomimosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous around 70 million years ago.

facts.statement: The first remains were discovered in 1965 in the Nemegt Formation of Mongolia.
facts.quote: In 1965, a pair of large arms, shoulder girdles, and a few other bones of a new dinosaur were first discovered in the Nemegt Formation of Mongolia.

facts.statement: Two additional complete specimens were described in 2014.
facts.quote: Two more complete specimens were described in 2014

facts.statement: Deinocheirus was the largest ornithomimosaur, reaching 11 meters in length and weighing 6.5 tons.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus was an unusual ornithomimosaur, the largest of the clade at 11 m long, and weighing 6.5 t.

facts.statement: Tall neural spines on its vertebrae formed a sail-like structure along its back.
facts.quote: Its vertebrae had tall neural spines that formed a "sail" along its back.

facts.statement: The skull was 1.024 meters long, featuring a wide bill and deep lower jaw similar to hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: The skull was 1.024 m long, with a wide bill and a deep lower jaw, similar to those of hadrosaurs.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus is thought to have been omnivorous, with evidence including plant indicators, fish scales, and gastroliths.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus is thought to have been omnivorous; its skull shape indicates a diet of plants, fish scales were found in association with one specimen and gastroliths were also present in the stomach region of the specimen.

facts.statement: The first remains were discovered by Zofia Kielan-Jaworowska on July 9, 1965.
facts.quote: The first known fossil remains of Deinocheirus were discovered by Polish palaeontologist Zofia Kielan-Jaworowska on July 9, 1965

facts.statement: The original specimen included both forelimbs (minus the right hand claws), shoulder girdle, three dorsal vertebrae, five ribs, gastralia, and two ceratobranchialia.
facts.quote: The specimen consisted of both forelimbs, excluding the claws of the right hand, the complete shoulder girdle, centra of three dorsal vertebrae, five ribs, gastralia (belly ribs), and two ceratobranchialia.

facts.statement: The holotype was originally catalogued as ZPal MgD-I/6 but is now re-catalogued as MPC-D 100/18.
facts.quote: The original specimen number of the holotype was ZPal MgD-I/6, but it has since been re-catalogued as MPC-D 100/18.

facts.statement: Additional elements of the holotype were announced in 2012 by Bell, Currie, and Lee.
facts.quote: In 2012, Phil R. Bell, Philip J. Currie, and Yuong-Nam Lee announced the discovery of additional elements of the holotype specimen

facts.statement: It is proposed that bite marks from Tarbosaurus caused the scattered state of the holotype specimen.
facts.quote: Bite marks on two gastralia were identified as belonging to Tarbosaurus, and it was proposed that this accounted for the scattered, disassociated state of the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus is classified as a primitive ornithomimosaurian closely related to Garudimimus and Beishanlong, forming the family Deinocheiridae.
facts.quote: After more complete remains were found, Deinocheirus was shown to be a primitive ornithomimosaurian, most closely related to the smaller genera Garudimimus and Beishanlong, together forming the family Deinocheiridae.

facts.statement: Two new Deinocheirus specimens were announced in 2013 at the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology conference by Lee, Barsbold, Currie, and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 2013, the discovery of two new Deinocheirus specimens were announced before the annual Society of Vertebrate Paleontology (SVP) conference by Lee, Barsbold, Currie, and colleagues.

facts.statement: The new Deinocheirus specimens were formally described in 2014 by Lee, Barsbold, Currie, Kobayashi, Hang-Jae Lee, Godefroit, Escuillié, and Chinzorig.
facts.quote: In 2014, the specimens were described by Lee, Barsbold, Currie, Yoshitsugu Kobayashi, Hang-Jae Lee Lee, Godefroit, Escuillié, and Tsogtbaatar Chinzorig.

facts.statement: Looted Deinocheirus fossils were repatriated to Mongolia on May 1, 2014, following a ceremony at the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.
facts.quote: On May 1, 2014, the fossils were repatriated to Mongolia by a delegation from the Belgian Museum, during a ceremony held at the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.

facts.statement: The reunited Deinocheirus skeleton is housed at the Central Museum of Mongolian Dinosaurs in Ulaanbaatar.
facts.quote: The reunited skeleton was deposited at the Central Museum of Mongolian Dinosaurs in Ulaanbaatar

facts.statement: Deinocheirus is the largest known ornithomimosaur, with the largest specimen estimated to be about 11 meters long and weigh 6.36 tons.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus is the largest ornithomimosaurian (ostrich dinosaur) discovered; according to the 2014 description, the largest known specimen measured about 11 m long, with an estimated weight of 6.36 t.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Deinocheirus length at 11.5 meters and mass at 5 tons in 2016.
facts.quote: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul presented a higher length estimate of 11.5 m but a lower mass estimate of 5 t.

facts.statement: Thomas R. Holtz estimated the length of Deinocheirus at 12 meters in 2012.
facts.quote: Holtz estimated the length of Deinocheirus at 12 m in 2012.

facts.statement: Campione and Evans estimated the body mass of Deinocheirus at approximately 6.5 to 7.3 tons in 2020.
facts.quote: In 2020, Campione and Evans gave a body mass estimate of approximately 6.5 t or 7.3 t depending on calculation method they used.

facts.statement: The only known Deinocheirus skull measures 1.024 meters in length from the premaxilla to the occipital condyle.
facts.quote: The only known skull, belonging to the largest specimen, measures 1.024 m from the premaxilla at the front to the back of the occipital condyle.

facts.statement: The Deinocheirus skull was low and narrow like other ornithomimosaurs, but featured a more elongated snout.
facts.quote: The skull was similar to those of other ornithomimosaurs in being low and narrow, but differed in that the snout was more elongated.

facts.statement: The bone walls of the Deinocheirus skull were very thin, measuring about 6 millimeters.
facts.quote: The skull bone walls were rather thin, about 6 mm.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus possessed a rounded, flattened beak that was covered by keratin during life.
facts.quote: It had a rounded, flattened beak, which would have been covered by keratin in life.

facts.statement: The Deinocheirus nostrils were directed upwards, and its nasal bone was a narrow strap extending above the eye sockets.
facts.quote: The nostrils were turned upwards, and the nasal bone was a narrow strap that extended up above the eye sockets.

facts.statement: The outer diameter of the Deinocheirus eye's scleral rings was 8.4 centimeters.
facts.quote: The outer diameter of the scleral rings in the eyes was small, 8.4 cm, compared to the size of the skull.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus had toothless, down-turned jaws, with a massive, deep lower jaw contrasting with a slender upper jaw.
facts.quote: The jaws were toothless and down-turned, and the lower jaw was very massive and deep compared to the slender and low upper jaw.

facts.statement: The Deinocheirus snout was spatulate and 25 centimeters wide, wider than the skull roof.
facts.quote: The snout was spatulate (flared outwards to the sides) and 25 cm wide, which is wider than the skull roof.

facts.statement: It is debated whether large tridactyl tracks found in the Nemegt locality were made by Deinocheirus, despite similarities to hadrosaur tracks and the lack of hadrosaur hand tracks.
facts.quote: Though the tracks were similar to those of hadrosaurs, no tracks of hadrosaur hands were identified, and since the feet of Deinocheirus are now known to have been similar to those of hadrosaurs, it cannot be ruled out that the tracks were made by this genus.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus and Therizinosaurus have the longest forelimbs of any known bipedal dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus and Therizinosaurus possessed the longest forelimbs known for any bipedal dinosaurs.

facts.statement: The holotype forelimbs of Deinocheirus measure 2.4 meters in total length, including 19.6 cm recurved claws.
facts.quote: The holotype forelimbs measure 2.4 m long – the humerus (upper arm bone) is 93.8 cm, the ulna 68.8 cm, and the hand is 77 cm – including the 19.6 cm recurved claws.

facts.statement: Each scapulocoracoid of the Deinocheirus shoulder girdle measures 1.53 meters in length.
facts.quote: Each scapulocoracoid of the shoulder girdle has a length of 1.53 m.

facts.statement: The Deinocheirus shoulder blade was long and narrow with a pronounced, triangular deltopectoralis crest.
facts.quote: The shoulder-blade was long and narrow, and the deltopectoralis crest was pronounced and triangular.

facts.statement: The ulna and radius of Deinocheirus were elongated and not firmly connected by a syndesmosis.
facts.quote: The ulna and radius (lower arm bones) were elongate and not firmly connected to each other in a syndesmosis.

facts.statement: Deep furrows on Deinocheirus arm bone articular surfaces indicate the presence of thick cartilage pads between the joints.
facts.quote: Most articular surfaces of the arm bones were deeply furrowed, indicating that the animal had thick pads of cartilage between the joints.

facts.statement: Despite being bulky, Deinocheirus had a narrow body indicated by its tall, relatively straight dorsal ribs.
facts.quote: Though Deinocheirus was a bulky animal, its dorsal ribs were tall and relatively straight, indicating that the body was narrow.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus had ten low, long neck vertebrae that resulted in an S-curved neck more pronounced than in other ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: The ten neck vertebrae were low and long, and progressively shorter backwards from the skull. This resulted in a more S-curved neck than seen in other ornithomimosaurs, due to the larger skull.

facts.statement: All Deinocheirus vertebrae were highly pneumatized by air sacs connected to the respiratory system, except for the atlas and hindmost tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: All the vertebrae were highly pneumatized by invading air sacs, except for the atlas bone and the hindmost tail-vertebrae, and were thereby connected to the respiratory system.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus possessed a U-shaped wishbone (furcula), a feature unknown in other ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: The wishbone (furcula), an element not known from any other ornithomimosaurs, was U-shaped.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus had relatively short hindlimbs where the femur was longer than the tibia, a trait common in large animals.
facts.quote: The hindlimbs were relatively short, and the thigh bone (femur) was longer than the shin bone (tibia), as is common for large animals.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus foot claws were blunt and broad-tipped, resembling large ornithischian unguals rather than the tapered claws of other theropods.
facts.quote: The claw bones of the feet were blunt and broad-tipped instead of tapered, unlike other theropods, but resembled the unguals of large ornithischian dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Osmólska and Roniewicz initially classified Deinocheirus in the new monotypic family Deinocheiridae within the infraorder Carnosauria.
facts.quote: Osmólska and Roniewicz initially concluded that Deinocheirus did not belong in any already named theropod family, so they created a new, monotypic family Deinocheiridae, placed in the infraorder Carnosauria.

facts.statement: In 1971, John Ostrom proposed that Deinocheirus belonged to Ornithomimosauria despite possessing both ornithomimosaurian and non-ornithomimosaurian characters.
facts.quote: In 1971, John Ostrom first proposed that Deinocheirus belonged with the Ornithomimosauria, while noting that it contained both ornithomimosaurian and non-ornithomimosaurian characters.

facts.statement: In 1976, Rhinchen Barsbold named the order Deinocheirosauria to include Deinocheirus and Therizinosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1976, Rhinchen Barsbold named the order Deinocheirosauria, which was to include the supposedly related genera Deinocheirus and Therizinosaurus.

facts.statement: A 2006 study suggested Deinocheirus was possibly the most primitive ornithomimosaur, though its exact affinities remained unresolved due to missing skull and hindlimb fossils.
facts.quote: A 2006 study by Kobayashi and Barsbold found Deinocheirus to be possibly the most primitive ornithomimosaur, but was unable to further resolve its affinities, due to the lack of skull and hindlimb elements.

facts.statement: A 2014 cladistic analysis grouped Deinocheirus with Garudimimus and Beishanlong into the family Deinocheiridae.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis accompanying the 2014 description of the two much more complete specimens found that Deinocheirus formed a clade with Garudimimus and Beishanlong, which were therefore included in the Deinocheiridae.

facts.statement: In 2020, Paraxenisaurus from Mexico was named as the first North American member of the Deinocheiridae group.
facts.quote: In 2020, the deinocheirid Paraxenisaurus from Mexico was named, making it the first member of the group known from North America.

facts.statement: While some writers supported a relationship between Deinocheirus and therizinosaurs, modern analysis does not consider them closely related.
facts.quote: A relationship between Deinocheirus and the long-armed therizinosaurs was supported by some later writers, but they are not considered to be closely related today.

facts.statement: Deinocheirids were not built for running, unlike other ornithomimosaurians.
facts.quote: Unlike other ornithomimosaurians, deinocheirids were not built for running.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Deinocheirus used its long arms and blunt claws for digging and gathering plants.
facts.quote: The blunt and short hand-claws of Deinocheirus were similar to those of the therizinosaur Alxasaurus, which indicates the long arms and claws were used for digging and gathering plants.

facts.statement: The blunt claws on Deinocheirus's feet may have prevented it from sinking into the substrate while wading.
facts.quote: The blunt claws of the feet could have helped the animal from sinking into substrate when wading.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus likely moved slowly, as indicated by its robust hind limbs and hip region.
facts.quote: The robust hind limbs and hip region indicates the animal moved slowly.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus's large size may have offered protection against predators like Tarbosaurus, but it sacrificed the running speed found in other ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: The large size of the animal may have protected it against predators such as Tarbosaurus, but in turn it lost the running ability of other ornithomimosaurs.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus was likely diurnal, as its relatively small scleral rings suggest it was active during the day.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus was likely diurnal (active during the day), since the scleral rings of the eyes were relatively small in comparison with its skull length.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus had a globular brain similar to birds and troodontids, with an expanded cerebrum and relatively large olfactory tracts.
facts.quote: The brain was globular and similar in shape to that of birds and troodontid theropods, the cerebrum was expanded in a way similar to most theropods, and the olfactory tracts were relatively large.

facts.statement: In 2015, Akinobu Watanabe and colleagues found that Deinocheirus, along with Archaeornithomimus and Gallimimus, had the most pneumatized skeletons among ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: In 2015, Akinobu Watanabe and colleagues found that together with Archaeornithomimus and Gallimimus, Deinocheirus had the most pneumatised skeleton among ornithomimosaurs.

facts.statement: The function of pneumatization in non-avian dinosaurs like Deinocheirus is not known with certainty, though it is advantageous for flight in modern birds.
facts.quote: Pneumatisation is thought to be advantageous for flight in modern birds, but its function in non-avian dinosaurs is not known with certainty.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus had a weak bite force, indicated by small muscle attachment sites relative to its skull size.
facts.quote: The attachment sites for the muscles that open and close the jaws were very small in comparison to the size of the skull, which indicates Deinocheirus had a weak bite force.

facts.statement: The presence of fish vertebrae and scales among gastroliths suggests Deinocheirus was an omnivore.
facts.quote: In spite of these features, fish vertebrae and scales were also found among the gastroliths, which suggests that it was an omnivore.

facts.statement: Researchers suspected Deinocheirus may have reverted to an omnivorous or carnivorous diet.
facts.quote: They suspected Deinocheirus may have reverted to omnivory/carnivory.

facts.statement: In their original description, Osmólska and Roniewicz suggested Deinocheirus's hands were unsuited for grasping but could have been used to tear prey apart.
facts.quote: In their original description, Osmólska and Roniewicz found that the hands of Deinocheirus were unsuited for grasping, but could instead have been used to tear prey apart.

facts.statement: In 1988, Paul suggested Deinocheirus's claws were too blunt for predation but would have served as good defensive weapons.
facts.quote: In 1988, Paul instead suggested that the claws were too blunt for predatory purposes, but would have been good defensive weapons.

facts.statement: In 2010, Phil Senter and James H. Robins suggested Deinocheirus specialized in eating high foliage due to its large hip height.
facts.quote: In 2010, Phil Senter and James H. Robins suggested that Deinocheirus had the largest vertical feeding range due to its hip height, and specialised in eating high foliage.

facts.statement: In 2017, it was suggested Deinocheirus's claws were adapted for pulling herbaceous plants out of water and reducing water resistance.
facts.quote: In 2017, it was suggested that the claws of Deinocheirus were adapted for pulling large quantities of herbaceous plants out of water, and to decrease the resistance of water.

facts.statement: Osmólska and Roniewicz reported paleopathologies in the holotype, including abnormal pits, grooves, and tubercles on the left second finger phalanges, possibly resulting from joint injuries.
facts.quote: Osmólska and Roniewicz reported palaeopathologies in the holotype specimen such as abnormal pits, grooves and tubercles on the first and second phalanx of the left second finger that may have been the result of injuries to the joint between the two bones.

facts.statement: The bite marks likely represent feeding behavior rather than aggression, suggesting Tarbosaurus focused on internal organs.
facts.quote: The bite marks probably represent feeding behaviour instead of aggression between the species, and the fact that bite marks were not found elsewhere on the body indicates the predator focused on internal organs.

facts.statement: The first remains of Deinocheirus were discovered in 1965 in the Nemegt Formation of Mongolia.
facts.quote: En 1965, un par de brazos grandes, fajas escapulares y algunos otros huesos de un nuevo dinosaurio se descubrieron por primera vez en la Formación Nemegt de Mongolia.

facts.statement: Two more complete specimens were described in 2014, providing new insights into the animal.
facts.quote: Se describieron dos especímenes más completos en 2014, que arrojan luz sobre muchos aspectos del animal.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 71 to 69 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 71 a 69 millones de años, entre el Campaniense y el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus was the largest ornithomimosaur, measuring 11 meters in length and weighing 6.36 tonnes.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus era un ornitomimosaurio inusual, el más grande del clado, con 11 metros de largo, y con 6,36 toneladas de peso.

facts.statement: Despite its large size, Deinocheirus had many hollow bones to reduce its weight.
facts.quote: Aunque era un animal voluminoso, tenía muchos huesos huecos que le ahorraban peso.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus possessed exceptionally large arms, up to 2.4 meters long, with three fingers ending in large, blunt claws.
facts.quote: Los brazos estaban entre los más grandes de cualquier dinosaurio bípedo de 2,4 metros de largo, con grandes y romas garras en sus manos de tres dedos.

facts.statement: High neural spines on its vertebrae formed a sail-like structure along its back.
facts.quote: Sus vértebras tenían altas espinas neurales que formaban una «vela» a lo largo de su espalda.

facts.statement: The tail ended in a pygostyle, suggesting the presence of a feather fan.
facts.quote: La cola termina en vértebras tipo pigostilo , que indican la presencia de un abanico de plumas.

facts.statement: Its skull was 1.024 meters long, featuring a wide beak and deep lower jaw similar to hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: Su cráneo medía 1,024 metros de largo, con un pico ancho y una mandíbula inferior profunda, similar a los de los hadrosáuridos .

facts.statement: Deinocheirus is classified as a primitive ornithomimosaur closely related to Garudimimus and Beishanlong, forming the family Deinocheiridae.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus ha demostrado ser un ornitomimosaurianos primitivo, más estrechamente relacionados con los géneros más pequeño Garudimimus y Beishanlong, formando juntos la familia Deinocheiridae.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus is believed to have been omnivorous, with a skull shape indicating a plant-based diet, supported by fish scales and gastrolites found with specimens.
facts.quote: Se cree que Deinocheirus fue omnívoro, su forma de cráneo indica una dieta de plantas, se encontraron escamas de peces en asociación con un espécimen y gastrolitos también estaban presentes en la región del estómago del espécimen.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the large claws may have been used for digging and collecting plants.
facts.quote: Las garras grandes pueden haber sido utilizadas para cavar y recolectar plantas.

facts.statement: Bite marks on Deinocheirus bones have been attributed to the tyrannosaurid Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: Las marcas de mordiscos en los huesos de Deinocheirus se han atribuido al tiranosáurido Tarbosaurus.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus is the largest discovered ornithomimosaur, with the largest known specimen reaching 11 meters in length and an estimated weight of 6.36 tonnes.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus es el ornitomimosaurio más grande descubierto, el espécimen más grande conocido mide hasta 11 metros de largo, con un peso estimado de 6,36 toneladas.

facts.statement: A 2010 study estimated the hip height of Deinocheirus to be between 3.3 and 3.6 meters.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2010 estimó que la altura de la cadera de Deinocheirus era de entre 3,3 a 3,6 metros.

facts.statement: The other two known specimens are smaller, with the holotype being 94% the size of the largest and the smallest, a subadult, being only 74% the size.
facts.quote: Los otros dos especímenes conocidos son más pequeños, el holotipo es el 94% del más grande y el más pequeño, un subadulto, solo el 74% del más grande.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus and Therizinosaurus possessed the longest known forelimbs of any bipedal dinosaur.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus y Therizinosaurus poseían las extremidades anteriores más largas conocidas para cualquier dinosaurio bípedo.

facts.statement: The holotype's forelimbs measured 2.4 meters long, with a 93.8 cm humerus, 68.8 cm ulna, and a 77 cm hand including 19.6 cm recurved claws.
facts.quote: Las extremidades anteriores del holotipo miden 2.4 metros de largo, el húmero, mide 93,8 centímetros, el cubito 68,8 centímetros y la mano 77 centímetros incluyendo las garras recurvadas largas de 19,6 centímetros.

facts.statement: Deinocheirus possessed a U-shaped furcula, a feature unknown in any other ornithomimosaur.
facts.quote: La furcula, un elemento no conocido de ningún otro ornitomimosaurianos, tenía forma de U.

facts.statement: Its hind legs were relatively short, with the femur longer than the tibia, a trait common in large animals.
facts.quote: Las patas traseras eran relativamente cortas y el hueso del muslo, el fémur era más largo que el hueso de la espinilla, la tibia, como es común para los animales grandes.

facts.statement: Despite its bulk, Deinocheirus had high, relatively straight dorsal ribs, indicating a narrow body.
facts.quote: Aunque Deinocheirus era un animal voluminoso, sus costillas dorsales eran altas y relativamente rectas, lo que indica que el cuerpo era estrecho.

facts.statement: The neural spines of the twelve dorsal vertebrae increased in length from front to back, with the last being 8.5 times the height of the vertebral centrum.
facts.quote: Las espinas neurales de las doce vértebras dorsales se hicieron cada vez más largas de craneal hacia caudal, siendo la última 8,5 veces la altura del centro vertebral.

facts.statement: All vertebrae were highly pneumatized with air sacs, except the atlas and the last tail vertebrae, connecting them to the respiratory system.
facts.quote: Todas las vértebras estaban altamente neumatizadas por los sacos de aire en su interior, a excepción del hueso atlas y las últimas vértebras de la cola, y por lo tanto estaban conectadas al sistema respiratorio.

facts.statement: The tail ended in at least two fused vertebrae described as similar to the pygostyles of oviraptorosaurian and therizinosaurian theropods.
facts.quote: La cola de Deinocheirus terminó en al menos dos vértebras fusionadas, que se describieron como similares al pigostilo de los terópodos oviraptorosaurianos y terizinosaurianos.

facts.statement: For nearly fifty years after the initial discovery, no further remains were found, and the animal's nature remained a mystery.
facts.quote: No se descubrieron más restos durante casi cincuenta años, y su naturaleza sigue siendo un misterio.

facts.statement: The only known skull of Deinocheirus measures 1.024 meters from the premaxilla to the back of the occipital condyle.
facts.quote: El único cráneo conocido, que pertenece al espécimen más grande, mide 1,024 metros desde el premaxilar hasta la parte posterior del cóndilo occipital.

facts.statement: The widest part of the skull behind the eyes is only 23 centimeters wide.
facts.quote: La parte más ancha del cráneo detrás de los ojos tiene solo 23 centímetros de ancho en comparación.

facts.statement: The skull was low and narrow like other ornithomimosaurians, but it differed by having a longer snout.
facts.quote: El cráneo era similar a los de otros ornitomimosaurios al ser bajo y angosto, pero difería en que el hocico era más alargado.

facts.statement: The skull bone walls were quite thin, approximately 6 millimeters thick.
facts.quote: Las paredes óseas del cráneo eran bastante delgadas, aproximadamente 6 milímetros.

facts.statement: It had a rounded, flattened beak that would have been covered by keratin when alive.
facts.quote: Tenía un pico redondeado y aplanado, que habría sido cubierto por la queratina en vida.

facts.statement: The outer diameter of the sclerotic rings in the eyes was small, 8.4 centimeters, compared to the skull size.
facts.quote: El diámetro exterior de los anillos escleróticos en los ojos era pequeño, 8,4 centímetros, en comparación con el tamaño del cráneo.

facts.statement: The jaws were toothless and turned downward, with the lower jaw being very large and deep compared to the thin, low upper jaw.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas eran desdentadas y giradas hacia abajo, y la mandíbula inferior era muy grande y profunda en comparación con la mandíbula superior delgada y baja.

facts.statement: The snout was spatulate and 25 centimeters wide, which is wider than the top of the skull.
facts.quote: El hocico era espatulado y de 25 centímetros de ancho, que es más ancho que el techo del cráneo.

facts.statement: The genus Deinocheirus was named by Kielan-Jaworowska in 1969.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Deinocheirus (genus), Kielan-Jaworowska 1969
